title: Shared definitions
description: Definitions shared by the policy, repo-overlay and work-order schemas. Not a schema for any one file.

mode.description: What an agent may do with a protected path. Tightening order: allow < ask < deny.

pathModes.description: The mode per session kind (spec §8.2): interactive = the operator is in the session; unattended = Hermes cron, webhook and API surfaces; workers = Pi or Claude Code inside Archon.

risk.description: A work order's risk: drives review depth and thresholds.

tier.description: An abstract model tier. Rosters map tiers to models; work orders and roles name tiers, never model ids.

sourceTier.description: A trusted-source tier (spec §10): T0 pinned local snapshots, T1 first-party domains and package registries, T2 curated aggregators, T3 the open web.

effort.description: Reasoning effort, using Archon's ladder; Archon clamps it to what each provider supports.

hostname.description: A plain, lowercase domain name with at least two labels: no scheme, port, path, wildcard or leading dot, and not an IP address. The egress generator allows the domain and its subdomains.

forgeHost.description: A forge host: one of the forge domains or a subdomain of one. The capture group is the forge domain. This is the one list of forge domains; src/policy/hosts.ts reads it from here.

nonForgeHost.description: A hostname that is not a forge host. Used wherever a host can reach the archon zone, which has no forge route (spec §4.3).

repoPath.description: A path or glob relative to the repo root: not absolute, not the root itself ('.', './'), no '..' segment, no backslash and no control character (U+0000-U+001F, U+007F-U+009F), as src/policy/paths.ts reads a path.

pathGlob.description: A protected-path glob, anchored at the repo root: segments joined by single slashes; '**' as a whole segment matches zero or more segments, '*' any run of characters within one segment, '?' exactly one; every other character is literal. No '.', '..' or empty segment, no leading or trailing slash, and no '[', ']', '{', '}', '!', backslash or control character, and printable ASCII only. Matching ignores case. A file's mode is the strictest across every glob that matches it (src/policy/paths.ts).

slug.description: Lowercase words joined by single hyphens, e.g. factory-task.

usd.description: An amount in US dollars, greater than zero.

exactVersion.description: An exact release version, MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (calendar versions such as 2026.10.24 too). Never a range (^4.3.0, ~4.3), a tag (latest) or a prerelease (4.3.0-canary.1).

advisoryId.description: A security advisory id: a CVE (CVE-2026-75130) or a GitHub advisory (GHSA-97r6-3rgm-v39r).

npmPin.description: An exact npm package pin: the name, an exact version and that version's registry integrity (dist.integrity at https://registry.npmjs.org/<name>, an SRI sha512). Shared by policy/mcp.yaml and policy/mcp.lock.json.

name.description: An npm package name, optionally scoped: @upstash/context7-mcp.

integrity.description: sha512- and 88 base64 characters, exactly as the registry gives it.

imagePin.description: An OCI image pinned by digest: name[:tag]@sha256:<64 hex>. A tag alone is not a pin.

httpsUrl.description: An https:// URL with no user info, whitespace or control characters.

mcpUrl.description: An MCP server's endpoint: an httpsUrl with no '$', query or fragment. Hermes expands ${VAR} and ${env:VAR} in a server entry's url, headers, args and env, so a '$' here could put Hermes's provider key, or another server's key, into a request to this host. A headers field, if one is ever added, gets the same ban. A query or fragment ('?', '#') could hold a literal credential (?key=...), which would be written in plaintext into every generated config. Shared by policy/mcp.yaml and policy/mcp.lock.json.
